data.narrative:
Kyoto Fusioneering is a Series C nuclear energy company founded by Satoshi Konishi, having raised $125M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a broader nuclear sector universe of 11 comparable companies: 3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

Only one valuation method proved applicable to this analysis. The stage-progression method, grounded in typical Series C step-up dynamics, applies a 1.7x multiplier to the $125M total raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $212M. A peer-median approach was not viable; while 6 same-sector peers exist, insufficient datapoints met narrow filtering criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-tier comps each returned fewer than 3 matches), making a narrow comp set median unreliable.

The analysis triangulates to a median valuation of $212M, with a range of $181M to $244M reflecting methodological constraints and stage-typical variance. Key uncertainties stem from the limited applicability of peer multiples in nuclear energy—a sector with few traded comparables and significant technology differentiation—and reliance on a single method. Investors should weight this valuation against specific risk factors: technology maturity, regulatory pathway clarity, and capital intensity of subsequent funding rounds.
